div.head: Hl 5[a]
div.ab: Gif frigman mannan forstele, gif he eft cuma stermelda, secge an andweardne; gecænne hine, gif he mæge: hæbbe þare freora rim æwdamanna ⁊ ænne mid in aþe, æghwilc man æt þam tune þe he tohyre;
Gif frigman mannan forstele, gif he eft cuma stermelda, secge an andweardne. Gecænne hine, gif he mæge: hæbbe þare freora rim æwda manna ⁊ ænne mid in aþe, æghwilc man, æt þam tune þe he tohyre;
Gif frigman mannan forstele, gif he eft cuma stermelda, secge an andweardne. Gecænne hine gif he mæge; hæbbe þare freora rim æwdamanna ⁊ ænne mid in aþe æghwilc man æt þam tune þe he tohyre.

Wenn ein Freier einen Menschen wegstiehlt, wenn [dann] dieser zurück [in die Heimath] kommt [als] Bestrafungsanzeiger, [so] klage [letzterer] gegen jenen persönlich; [der Menschendieb] reinige sich [von dieser Klage], wenn er kann: er habe solcher Freier eine Anzahl [als] Eidesmannen und [zwar] einen mit im Eide, jeglichen [Eides]mann aus dem Ortsbezirk, welchem er [selbst] zugehört;

If a freeman steals away a person, if [then] this person comes back [home] [as] accuser for punishment, [then] let [the latter] bring the charge against him in person; let [the man-thief] clear himself [of this charge], if he can: let him have a number of such freemen [as] oath-men, and [indeed] one with him in the oath, each [oath-]man from the local district to which he [himself] belongs;

If a freeman steals a man, and if he [who has been stolen] returns as informer, he shall accuse him to his face; and he [the thief] shall clear himself if he can. And every man involved in such a charge shall have a number of free witnesses, and one [at least] of his witnesses from the village to which he himself belongs.

If a freeman steals a man, if the latter comes back as informer, he is to accuse him to his face; he is to clear himself, if he can; each man [so charged] is to have a number of free oath-helpers, and one with him in the oath from the village to which he belongs; if he cannot do that, he is to pay as he can afford.

If a freeman steals a person, if he afterwards comes as an informer, let him announce it in the presence [of the thief]. Let him [the man accused] clear himself if he is able; let each man [so charged] have a number of free oathmen and one with [him] in the oath from the dwelling to which he belongs.

note.seg: Im Sinne von ‘jemand’; vgl. Wb frigman 3
In the sense of ‘anyone’; cf. Wb frigman 3
S. Gl Menschenraub 2. Vgl. bei anderen Germanen Brunner I² 433²⁹. II 639; Wilda 797
See Gl Menschenraub 2. Cf. among other Germanic peoples Brunner I² 433²⁹. II 639; Wilda 797
eft heisst öfter ‘zurück’ in Verb. mit ‘kommen, kehren, gehen’; Toller Suppl. s. v.
eft often means ‘back’ in combination with ‘come, turn, go’; Toller Suppl. s. v.

Die Endung -a bezeichnet 12. Jh.; s. Wb 39 Sp. 1. — Grimm lehnte Prices Übs. ‘to denounce him before the stermelda’ ab (Kl. Schr. V 320). In letzterem erblickten Frühere einen öffentlichen Ankläger, oder (an steor Steuer denkend) ‘exactor tributi’, einen Fiskalvogt, im Sinne des späteren Sheriff; Robertson Hist. essays 115 De Læt wollte gar ær melda ‘antequam accusator poscat responsum’ ändern

The ending -a indicates the 12th cent.; see Wb 39 col. 1. — Grimm rejected Price’s transl. ‘to denounce him before the stermelda’ (Kl. Schr. V 320). In the latter earlier scholars saw a public prosecutor, or (thinking of steor ‘tax’) ‘exactor tributi’, a fiscal reeve, in the sense of the later sheriff; Robertson Hist. essays 115 De Læt even wanted to emend to ær melda ‘antequam accusator poscat responsum’
Vgl. he hire ondweardre to spræce; him ondweardum secgan ‘angesichts ihrer, seiner’; Agsä. Bede IV 8. 25 ed. Miller p. 286. 344
Cf. he hire ondweardre to spræce; him ondweardum secgan ‘in her, his presence’; A.-S. Bede IV 8. 25 ed. Miller p. 286. 344
Diese Bedingung, obwohl überflüssig, ist in Gesetzen häufig; z. B. Hl 7. 16, 1. Af 22
This condition, though superfluous, is frequent in laws; e.g. Hl 7. 16, 1. Af 22
‘beschaffe, erbringe, stelle’; s. Wb: habban 3
‘procure, produce, provide’; see Wb: habban 3

Die Endung in þare ist mittelenglisch — ebenso Wi 8 —, also keine Emendation zu þær angebracht. — Bed. ‘besagter’; s. Wb: ‘Demonstrativ’ I 1. — Die Eideshelfer (s. d. Gl 14f.) müssen vom Stande des Hauptschwörers sein

The ending in þare is Middle English — likewise Wi 8 —, so no emendation to þær is called for. — Meaning ‘the said’; see Wb: ‘Demonstrativ’ I 1. — The oath-helpers (see that word in Gl 14f.) must be of the rank of the principal swearer

Wilkins (und Schmid) erdenkt ein [unmögliches] Adj. rimæwda; Schmid verbindet es mit rimað, streicht and und lässt den Gen. manna von ænne abhängen. Allein and ist durch Wi 19 gesichert. — Freora erklärt sich aus Gl eidesfähig 1a. Dafür wollten Frühere feowra aus Wi 21 oder þreora sum emendieren; dann wäre doch ‘4 oder 3 Eideshelfer’ einfacher gewesen. — Vielmehr steht rim, der Kreis der möglichen, im Ggs. zum wirklichen Eideshelfer; s. d. Gl 21f. Toller zitiert: rim manna, wera rim; of heora rime gemetfæstne man übersetzt ex suo numero virum modestum. Das Fehlen der Zahl möglicher Eideshelfer braucht nicht auf dem Überspringen eines Wortes in der Überlieferung zu beruhen. Sie stand vielleicht fest: etwa 12, wie im Volleide benachbarter Germanen; Brunner II 384; Sohm Fränk. Reichsvf. 581. Oder aber sie ward tatsächlich durchs Gericht bestimmt. Da 2 wohl nicht schon rim bildeten, waren 3 Minimum, wie denn in Wi 21 der vierhändige der normale Eid des Freien ist

Wilkins (and Schmid) invents an [impossible] adj. rimæwda; Schmid connects it with rimað, deletes and and makes the gen. manna depend on ænne. But and is secured by Wi 19. — Freora is explained by Gl eidesfähig 1a. Earlier scholars wanted to emend it to feowra from Wi 21, or to þreora sum; but then ‘4 or 3 oath-helpers’ would surely have been simpler. — Rather, rim, the circle of possible oath-helpers, stands in contrast to the actual oath-helper; see that word in Gl 21f. Toller cites: rim manna, wera rim; of heora rime gemetfæstne man translated ex suo numero virum modestum. The absence of the number of possible oath-helpers need not be due to a word having been skipped in the transmission. It was perhaps fixed: say 12, as in the full oath of neighbouring Germanic peoples; Brunner II 384; Sohm Fränk. Reichsvf. 581. Or else it was in practice determined by the court. Since 2 probably did not yet constitute a rim, 3 were the minimum, just as in Wi 21 the four-handed oath is the normal oath of the freeman

on aðe beon heisst ‘wirklich als Eideshelfer (s. d. Gl 47) fungieren’, im Ggs. zum blossen Bereitstehen dafür. Da sowohl rim wie ænne Objekt zu habbe ist, bestimmt also Beklagter den Kreis wie den wirklichen Helfer; es liegt also nicht ‘Auswahleid’ (s. d. Gl) vor. — Eín Eideshelfer (s. d. Gl 33a) kommt auch sonst vor

on aðe beon means ‘actually to act as oath-helper (see that word in Gl 47)’, as opposed to merely standing ready to do so. Since both rim and ænne are objects of habbe, the defendant thus determines both the circle and the actual helper; this is therefore not a ‘selection oath’ (see that word in Gl). — A single oath-helper (see that word in Gl 33a) occurs elsewhere too
Nachbarschaft ist eine oft geforderte Qualität der Eideshelfer; s. d. Gl 10. Trenne im Texte to hyre; von Präp. to hängt vorhergehendes þe ab
Neighbourhood is a frequently required qualification of oath-helpers; see that word in Gl 10. In the text divide to hyre; the preceding þe depends on the prep. to
For the ‘number’ we may possibly compare Wiht. cap. 21.

Liebermann takes this sentence to mean that every witness must belong to the same village as the accused (er habe solcher Freier eine Anzahl [als] Eidesmannen und [zwar] einen mit im Eide, jeglichen [Eides]mann aus dem Ortsbezirk, welchem er [selbst] zugehört); but æghwilc is nominative, not accusative.
Lit. ‘one [of those] in oath with [him].’
The order of words is awkward, as not unfrequently in Anglo-Saxon, e.g. Sax. Chron. ann. 878: ⁊ hiene mon þær ofslog, ⁊ dccc monna mid him. ⁊ xl monna his heres.

note.label: belongs
note.seg: This is a difficult clause. With Attenborough I take æghwilc man “each man”, since it is nominative, to be the subject, in spite of its late place in the sentence. Liebermann refers it to all the oath-helpers, making it requisite that all should come from his own village, and thinks that the accused is to have a number of these present, but swear with only one of them.

note.label: afford
note.seg: The MS. gono hage is normally amended to genoh age to give this sense. The copyist may have been influenced by the verb onhagian which can mean “to afford”. Presumably if the accused had not enough he would suffer other penalties. This law is altogether rather vague, leaving the number of oath-helpers unspecified also.

note.label: before: Gif
note.seg: This line extends into the left margin.

note.label: he
note.seg: It is not clear whether ‘he’ refers to the stolen person, presumably a slave, or to his owner. See Commentary under ‘Oath supporters.’

note.label: informer,
note.seg: Stermelda only occurs here, and the first element is obscure, so it is difficult to interpret precisely, although the second element, melda, clearly means ‘informer.’ Bosworth emends the compound to stelmelda, ‘informer about the theft,’ which gives a satisfactory meaning in context, but postulates that this careful scribe would have committed the unusual error of copying l for r. If we play on the e/æ variation found so frequently in Hloþhere & Eadric (see ‘Some notes on the language’) we might get stærmelda, ‘informer about [this] history’; I am uncomfortable with this suggestion, however, as the use of stær- generally implies a history grander in scope than the personal realm. It seems likely that the general meaning is ‘open accuser,’ as Liebermann, Gesetze, 3:29 suggests; pending a more conclusive analysis of the first element, I have chosen to translate only the second.
